title: A Flash First, Full Story Only When You Stop | vitalii.no
description:
The guide used to write and queue a full story for every named place near the car's GPS position, whether or not the road actually passed it. That meant hearing stories about places across a valley that were never part of the route, and no warning before a story started — it just began mid-sentence whenever the app decided to play it.

A new on-route flag now marks a place as relevant only when it sits within 150 meters of the actual matched street path the car drove (900 meters for villages and lakes). The Android side computes live speed and heading to fire a short distance cue first — in 200 metres, right — timed to land right as the car arrives, followed by a one-sentence flash clip instead of jumping straight into full narration.

Full narration now only starts once the car has stayed within 120 meters of a place for at least 8 seconds below about 15 km/h, and fades out over 3 seconds if the car pulls away. Places that were never on the route stopped getting stories at all.
